title: RunnerRunRecord
description:
The run record `agent-runner` returns from `POST /dispatch` and lists/serves from `GET /runs` / `GET /runs/{id}` (agent-runner's own `RunRecord`, `src/domain/run.ts`). Fulfils demand `factory-20260911-interface-extraction` criterion 2, and (for `dispatchKey` and `workspace`) demand `agent-runner-20260927-contracts-runner-keyed-dispatch` — additive only, copied from the real, shipped TypeScript type, not invented ahead of it.

**Receipt semantics.** This record — specifically `state`, `exitCode`, `transcriptPath` and (via `runner.transcript-snapshot.json`) the normalized transcript it is served alongside — is the ONLY authoritative receipt that a dispatch happened and how it ended. An HTTP error from `POST /dispatch` does not prove no run started (the request can fail after the runner already accepted it); absence of a matching record in `GET /runs` is likewise never proof of non-dispatch, only 'no evidence yet' (`factory.service.reconcile`'s own comment: 'Absence/ambiguity never proves no dispatch occurred').

**Stable operation correlation.**

- **Keyed (preferred).** When the run was dispatched with a `dispatchKey`, it is echoed here and the run is resolvable directly at `GET /dispatches/{dispatchKey}` — see `runner.dispatch-reservation.json`. That lookup returns this record, so a lost `POST /dispatch` response needs no scan at all.
- **Unkeyed (fallback).** A caller that embedded its own operation token as the first line of `prompt` at dispatch time (see `runner.dispatch-request.json`) re-identifies its run by finding the single record whose `id` equals the id returned at dispatch, OR whose `prompt` starts with `"<token>\n"`. Zero or ambiguous (>1) matches are both 'still uncertain, do not resend'; only exactly one match is a resolved receipt.

**Producer-result lookups.** This record is what `agent-runner` serves a normalized `delivery.producer-result` for, at `GET /runs/{id}/producer-result` and — when the run was keyed — `GET /dispatches/{dispatchKey}/producer-result`. Both return `delivery.producer-result`; `correlation.operationKey` carries this record's `dispatchKey` when it has one, and `null` otherwise. `workspace` is what makes the result revision-bound: see that field.

id.description: This run's own identifier, minted by agent-runner at dispatch time.

prompt.description: The exact prompt this run was dispatched with — what a caller matches its own operation token against for correlation (see top-level description).

dispatchKey.description: Echoed verbatim from the `POST /dispatch` request when the run was keyed; ABSENT (not null) when the run was unkeyed, including every run recorded before this field existed. The key is the caller's, so this is a correlation echo, not a runner-minted identity — `id` remains the run's own identity and the two are never interchangeable. `same key + same requestHash` returns the SAME run id here (a replay), never a second run; the key is bound to exactly one run id for its lifetime, and a run that ends `failed` with `exitCode: null` after an uncertain dispatch stays bound to it — it is never relaunched automatically under the same key.

state.description: Lifecycle state. Same enum as `state.event.json`'s `AgentRunPayload.phase` (agent-runner's own `RunState` is, at the type level, a direct alias of it — the two can never drift apart). `launched` is the only non-terminal value; `finished`/`failed`/`stopped` are all terminal. A caller reconciling a dispatch treats any OTHER apparent value, or no matching record, as still unresolved — never as evidence of failure.

exitCode.description: The dispatched process's exit code; `null` while `state` is `launched`, or if the process never produced one (e.g. `stopped`/timed-out).

timedOut.description: True if the run was ended by the runner's own wall-clock timeout rather than the process exiting on its own.

stopped.description: True if the run was ended by an explicit `POST /runs/{id}/stop` rather than exiting or timing out.

transcriptPath.description: Server-local path to this run's raw transcript file. Opaque to a remote caller — use `GET /runs/{id}` for the normalized view (`runner.transcript-snapshot.json`), never this path directly.

tokensUsed.description: Total tokens consumed, parsed from the CLI's own terminal result line. Sum of `tokensIn`/`tokensOut` when both are present.

model.description: The model the CLI itself reported actually running — parsed from its own init line, so it reflects reality even when it differs from a requested `model` override.

runtime.description: Name of the runtime profile this run actually dispatched on.

usageProvider.description: The `usage.event` provider string denormalized at dispatch time from the resolved runtime profile — describes the dimension in force when the run happened, immune to later config edits.

workspace.title: RunnerRunWorkspace
workspace.description:
The runner's OWN git observation of the run's workspace (`src/domain/workspace.ts`): what the repo looked like immediately before launch and immediately after the process exited. **This is machine observation, never the agent's claim** — the runner reads it from the workspace itself while it still holds the repo's one-live-session lock, and it never takes it from the report or the transcript (D113: a transcript statement is `worker-claim` only). This is what makes a `delivery.producer-result` revision-bound and lets Factory refuse to accept a dirty tree's `HEAD` as the revision the run produced.

OPTIONAL, and `null` (or absent) means **not observed at all** — never a guess and never a default. Absent on runs recorded before this field existed. Every branch and revision field is `null` when it could not be observed (not a git repo, git failed or timed out, detached HEAD for the branch fields), and `dirty: null` means the dirty state itself was unobservable — which a consumer must treat as dirty, not as clean.

The two observations are flattened onto this one object: `baseBranch`/`baseRevision` are the pre-launch (`base`) observation, `branch`/`revision`/`dirty` are the post-exit (`head`) observation. `observedAt` is when the observation behind `branch`/`revision`/`dirty` was taken. A run the runner could not supervise to exit (an orphan reconciled at startup after a restart) has no post-exit observation at all: those three stay `null` and only the `base` pair is populated — reading the repo later could see another worker's changes, so the runner does not pretend to have looked.

baseBranch.description: Checked-out branch short name observed immediately BEFORE the process was launched; `null` on detached HEAD or when unobservable.

baseRevision.description: Full 40-hex lowercase `HEAD` SHA observed immediately BEFORE the process was launched; `null` when unobservable. A short SHA, a tag, a branch name or any uppercase hex is NOT this value.

branch.description: Checked-out branch short name observed immediately AFTER the process exited, while the runner still held the repo lock; `null` on detached HEAD, when unobservable, or when the run was never supervised to exit.

revision.description: Full 40-hex lowercase `HEAD` SHA observed immediately AFTER the process exited, while the runner still held the repo lock; `null` when unobservable or when the run was never supervised to exit. **`HEAD` is only the run's produced revision when `dirty` is `false`** — a dirty tree's `HEAD` does not contain what the run produced, so a consumer must map a dirty or unobservable revision to a `null` revision rather than accept this value blindly.

dirty.description: True when tracked files were modified relative to `HEAD` at the post-exit observation (untracked files ignored). `null` means the dirty state itself was unobservable — treat that as dirty, never as clean.

observedAt.description: When the observation behind `branch`/`revision`/`dirty` was taken. `null` only when nothing at all was observed (`workspace` itself would normally just be `null` in that case; both spellings mean the same absence).

error.description: Present when `state` is `failed` — a short description of the failure.
